title: Coordinate one inherited Learning repair — plan 001
epic_title: Coordinate one repair for inherited Learning evidence failures

tasks.title: Share the existing evidence report and witness predicate
tasks.goal: Orchestration can consume the existing typed evidence report and witness-mismatch predicate without duplicating or weakening them.
tasks.current: The evidence report types and witness predicate are private to the memory CLI.
tasks.desired: A reusable typed codec and predicate retain the current report schema, exact mismatch requirements, and verified-successor classification; the ordinary verifier consumes the same definitions.
scope: Extract the report types, closed decoding boundary, and witness predicate as the prerequisite refactor.
Preserve report fields, serialization, classification, and existing gate behavior.
Keep fetching, task creation, and model execution outside the evidence verifier.
out_of_scope: New evidence exceptions, new record kinds, repair orchestration, or a corpus migration.
acceptance: Existing evidence report fixtures remain byte-equivalent and the current verified-successor refusal suite passes.
The shared predicate accepts only invalid content or membership mismatches with a witnessed snapshot and rejects empty or mixed unsupported findings.
The shared report decoder rejects malformed or unknown fields and exposes the same predecessor and verified successor identities used by the CLI.
key_interfaces: memory-evidence-report/v1, record identity and digest, evidence entries, witness mismatch, and verified successor fields.

implementation.rationale: Extract the existing report codec and exact witness predicate without moving orchestration into evidence validation or changing verdicts.

review.rationale: The review must prove that extraction preserves every existing evidence refusal and the narrow verified-successor exception.

tasks.title: Verify a freshly fetched target with its pinned tool
tasks.goal: A caller obtains one current target snapshot and its compatible evidence verdict without altering its working checkout.
tasks.current: Local memory checks use the caller's available checkout and verifier; there is no repair-specific fresh-target inspection boundary.
tasks.desired: A context-aware inspection port returns the freshly observed target commit, canonical repository identity, retained evidence, and verifier identity from isolated storage, or an explicit unavailable-prerequisite result.
scope: Fetch the configured target and required retained history into isolated storage, with cleanup owned by the invocation.
Run the target's source-mode or verified release-mode tool through strict existing resolution and parse its typed evidence report.
Bind all inspection data to one target commit and verifier identity; require a fresh remote observation even when reusable proof exists.
out_of_scope: Another installer or compatibility service, shared repair mutations, and automatic updates to caller branches.
acceptance: A stale local remote-tracking ref and older caller tool still produce the current remote target verdict through the target-selected verifier.
Fetch or retained-history failure returns freshness_unknown; unavailable or incompatible pinned tooling returns verifier_unavailable; neither path invokes a tracker or executor.
Source-mode and release-mode fixtures reject ambient-tool fallback and report the exact target and verifier used.
Success, failure, and cancellation preserve caller HEAD, index, tracked modifications, and untracked files and clean up owned temporary state.
key_interfaces: Context-aware target inspection, canonical repository binding, strict tool resolution, target commit, verifier identity, and typed evidence report.

implementation.rationale: Compose isolated Git history, target-owned source or release pins, strict tool resolution, and typed verification without touching caller state.

review.rationale: A stale cache, ambient tool fallback, or mixed target snapshot could authorize an incorrect repair or false adoption result.

tasks.title: Admit only the verified inherited Learning incident
tasks.goal: Requests naming the same verified inherited Learning converge on one identity, while unsupported or already-resolved cases produce a non-mutating result.
tasks.current: There is no incident-scoped request admission or shared identity derived from verified caller and target evidence.
tasks.desired: One explicit Learning ID identifies the candidate; the core verifies the caller's committed object and fresh target, then yields a deterministic admission or a typed refusal/adoption result.
scope: Validate one literal Learning ID and actual committed caller record bytes under the operator's input ruling (problem:inherited-learning-repair#A-7); the entry does not extract identities from prose or caller-supplied report files.
Require unchanged frozen target bytes, complete history, valid store and relations, durable evidence, and only the existing supported witness mismatch.
Derive identity from the configured canonical repository and Learning ID; witness paths, wording, machines, and caller commits remain evidence only.
Detect the verified successor at the pinned target; return update_required, or revalidate an already-current caller before returning healthy or unsupported_case.
out_of_scope: Query or report-file input, fuzzy matching, other memory failures, mutation of frozen records, and creation of tasks or refs.
acceptance: Different diagnostics, witnesses, machines, and caller revisions naming the same explicit Learning ID yield one identity and admit only the unchanged inherited Learning.
Missing, malformed or multiple IDs, wrong kinds, changed or new records, missing history, invalid relations, and other evidence codes refuse with zero shared effects.
A verified successor returns the full current target and successor identity with an adoption instruction; an already-current caller is healthy only after its own relevant check passes.
Instructions embedded in verifier diagnostics or record content cannot change repository bindings, execute a command, select tool policy, or authorize a predecessor rewrite.
key_interfaces: Verified caller snapshot, admission identity, memory-evidence-report/v1, learning-repair-result/v1, and typed refusal/adoption outcomes.

implementation.rationale: Exact identity, caller-object verification, inherited-byte comparison, and successor adoption form a bounded deterministic decision.

review.rationale: Review must reject unsupported findings and adversarial report text while preserving stale-caller adoption without shared writes.

tasks.title: Reserve one persistent repair across independent callers
tasks.goal: Independent callers reserve or join the same durable operation before any tracker or executor effect.
tasks.current: The reusable Git-ref store supplies compare-and-swap, but there is no Learning repair record or ownership protocol.
tasks.desired: RepairStore atomically creates the incident's fixed ref and validates the closed learning-repair/v1 state on every read and owner-authorized transition; losing callers observe the winner.
scope: Implement the exact incident ref namespace and versioned record with repository, Learning digest, target, verifier, owner token, phase, and optional canonical references.
Reuse Git-ref compare-and-swap for create-if-absent and conditional updates; re-read a winning generation after contention.
Validate identity, owner, and allowed transitions, retaining terminal and uncertain operations indefinitely.
Provide read-only joining and preserve pre-effect phases when execution stops; expose no lease expiry, takeover, or retry policy.
out_of_scope: Tracker creation, executor dispatch, crash recovery, and trusting task-search similarity for ownership.
acceptance: Five independent processes using separate checkouts and one bare remote produce one ref and one owner; every loser reads that same operation.
Foreign repository or Learning identity, digest mismatch, unknown JSON fields, malformed records, wrong owner, and illegal transitions refuse without mutation.
A stale compare-and-swap cannot overwrite the winner, and an unsupported atomic-ref capability refuses rather than using a local mutex for correctness.
Failed, uncertain, terminal, and indefinitely reserved operations remain observable and cannot cause another reservation or owner takeover.
key_interfaces: RepairStore, learning-repair/v1, create-if-absent, observed-head compare-and-swap, owner token, and the contract's phase enum.

implementation.rationale: Reuse remote compare-and-swap while enforcing winner ownership, immutable operation identity, and closed phase transitions across processes.

review.rationale: The critical failure is two live owners or a retry that repeats an external effect; review requires independent-process contention and corrupt-state cases.

tasks.title: Create the canonical tracker task once
tasks.goal: The live owner creates one understandable task through the configured tracker, and every joining caller receives its canonical reference.
tasks.current: Tracker adapters can create work items, but creation is not guarded by a shared Learning repair reservation.
tasks.desired: After a fresh post-reservation predicate check, the owner persists creating_task before one create request and records task_ready with the exact returned source reference; failures remain on that operation.
scope: Introduce the consumer-owned context-aware TaskCreator and adapt the existing GitHub, Forgejo, and Carina creation capabilities.
Render identity, target evidence, intended lesson, bounded correction scope, acceptance, and an operation marker into the canonical task.
Recheck the target immediately before creation; a concurrently landed fix produces the no-work/adoption result without creating a task.
Distinguish definite failure from outcome uncertainty; never retry creation from a subsequent caller or add generic fleet-discovery routing.
out_of_scope: New tracker implementations, task-description similarity, dispatch, and uncertain-effect recovery.
acceptance: Adapter conformance for all configured tracker families shows one creation after creating_task, exact task readback, required evidence/acceptance, and zero creations from joiners.
A fix landing after reservation but before creation yields adoption instructions and zero task creation.
A definite create error records failed; an ambiguous result records outcome_unknown when persistence is available, otherwise retains creating_task; later callers never retry.
Provider credentials and local user paths stay out of persisted state and task text, and labels cannot start an independent fleet attempt.
key_interfaces: TaskCreator, configured tracker binding, canonical task source reference, operation marker, and creating_task/task_ready transitions.

implementation.rationale: Compose configured existing tracker creation adapters with the reserved operation, a last fresh-target check, and one self-contained task.

review.rationale: Review must prove no duplicate creation after ambiguity and no discovery label that launches a second worker outside direct admission.

tasks.title: Dispatch one bounded successor correction through implement-now
tasks.goal: The canonical task reaches the existing direct-issue executor exactly once under a frozen successor-repair charter.
tasks.current: Direct-issue admission and per-task claims exist, but no repair owner creates their incident-specific input or records their outcome.
tasks.desired: The owner inspects the exact task fingerprint, builds issue-task-input/v1 with separate derived implementation/review requirements, persists dispatching, and owns one foreground executor process based on the inspected target.
scope: Render a structured native charter that verifies the intended lesson, preserves the predecessor, uses the coded successor writer, and requires ordinary gates and independent review.
Reuse exact issue admission, configured routing, and the executor's existing task claim; pass a trusted repair handle independently of quoted diagnostic prose for the worker integration to consume.
Recheck the starting target before correction and close out as no-work if the correction already landed; unsupported evidence blocks rather than inventing a successor.
Record launch results and exact proposal references through running and awaiting_merge, with failed or uncertain outcomes retained without redispatch.
out_of_scope: Another executor, hard-coded model choices, evidence allowances, autonomous merge, and declaring a green proposal resolved.
acceptance: The incident task is admitted from its exact fingerprint and role requirements and launches one foreground executor; five callers or a changed source fingerprint cannot launch another.

The charter requires unchanged predecessor bytes and original witness, a verified superseding Learning, ordinary checks, independent review, and blocking when retained evidence cannot support the correction.
Launch failure or ambiguity retains failed, outcome_unknown, or the durable pre-effect phase with no later retry; an executor result records its exact proposal without asserting resolution.

The executor invocation carries the trusted repair context; diagnostic text cannot supply that context, alter policy, or escape the inspected-target workspace. Worker recognition and recursive suppression are verified in T9.
key_interfaces: issue-task-input/v1, issue inspection fingerprint, native task requirements, direct-issue admission and claim, trusted repair context, and foreground executor receipts.

implementation.rationale: Bind an exact tracker snapshot to a frozen native charter, configured role requirements, isolated execution, and one owner-controlled launch.

review.rationale: The executor boundary must preserve independent review and merge authority while preventing prompt injection, duplicate launch, and recursive repair.

tasks.title: Wait for verified landing and report caller adoption
tasks.goal: A joining caller follows one repair and receives a verified target to adopt without starting work or changing its checkout.
tasks.current: There is no shared repair wait interface or target-verified completion predicate for blocked callers.
tasks.desired: Cancellable polling exposes canonical references as available, verifies current target content before adoption, and reports unresolved terminal state without redispatch.
scope: Poll the operation at an injected five-second default and expose phase and task/proposal references without claiming that a stored phase proves liveness.
While awaiting merge, freshly observe target identity and reuse evidence only for the identical target/verifier pair within the invocation.
Return the full verified target, successor, and rerun instruction after landing; preserve separate caller revalidation.
Cancel only the waiting caller and retain terminal, failed, uncertain, or stalled operations without takeover.
out_of_scope: Modifying caller branches, automatic retries, owner cancellation by a waiter, and treating host status as resolution.
acceptance: Open or green proposals and closed tasks never resolve a repair; a fetched target with the verified successor returns update_required and a rerun instruction.
Unchanged target/verifier pairs reuse verification after a fresh remote read; changed targets reverify, and remote-read failure returns freshness_unknown instead of cached success.
Cancelled wait returns its handle promptly, leaves the operation intact, and permits another waiter to continue without extra tasks or launches.
A terminal operation whose target still fails returns unresolved with the same task; failed, uncertain, and stalled records never trigger another attempt.
key_interfaces: Cancellable waiter, injected poll cadence, fresh target identity, exact-target verification cache, repair handle, and adoption result.

implementation.rationale: Combine cancellable observation with fresh target identity and reuse proof only within the exact target/verifier pair.

review.rationale: Review must distinguish a green proposal, shared resolution, and caller readiness and reject stale success during remote failure.

tasks.title: Expose explicit repair and bounded scan through the memory CLI
tasks.goal: Agents and existing daily triggers invoke the same bounded repair behavior through the advertised memory command.
tasks.current: The memory CLI exposes evidence checks but no explicit repair, shared wait, or incident scan.
tasks.desired: Under the operator's input ruling (problem:inherited-learning-repair#A-7), the command composes configured ports, accepts either one `--record Learning-<ULID>` or `--scan`, supports wait and JSON results, and reports supported no-work and refusal outcomes without another agent loop.
scope: Wire the existing memory dispatch and source/installed tool flow to the repair core, keeping adapter imports in composition roots.
Expose one explicit Learning ID or a mutually exclusive scan, wait, help, and learning-repair-result/v1 output with the contract's outcome and reference fields.
Scan one pinned target for supported unresolved Learnings, then use the same fresh admission path for each and await only its own foreground dispatch completion.
Emit EVT-1 through structured logging without raw diagnostics, credentials, or user paths.
out_of_scope: Query or report-file input, a scheduler, automatic schedule registration, broader diagnosis, and automatic worker delegation.
acceptance: Built CLI and installed exec-flow fixtures cover admission, join, update_required, healthy, refusals, cancellation, failed, uncertain, and unresolved outcomes with valid versioned JSON and non-JSON help.
Empty scan makes zero tracker or executor calls; a scan racing agent intake joins the same operation and does not wait for human merge.
Missing or conflicting record/scan operands, malformed or multiple IDs, removed `--query`/`--report` flags, other unknown flags, and unavailable configured adapters refuse before shared effects.
The CLI uses the configured host, tracker, and executor, emits bounded EVT-1 fields, and performs no inference before the single admitted dispatch.
key_interfaces: memory repair operand grammar, scan and wait modes, CLI dependency injection, learning-repair-result/v1, and EVT-1.

implementation.rationale: Wire the bounded orchestration into the existing command and configured adapters, including scan composition and machine-readable results.

review.rationale: Review must prove explicit, installed, and scan entry points share admission and never silently select a provider, retry an effect, or wait for human merge during a scan.

tasks.title: Delegate the worker's known blocker without a local repair loop
tasks.goal: An opted-in worker blocked by this inherited Learning delegates to the shared operation instead of independently editing memory.
tasks.current: Local and hosted CI recovery can launch independent fixers for a memory-gate failure.
tasks.desired: A closed optional memory.inherited_learning_repair.enabled boolean defaults false; when enabled, structured incident diagnostics reach shared admission, admitted/joining workers suspend their memory-fixing loop, and adoption returns a typed task blocker.
scope: Add the closed opt-in setting without enabling it in repository defaults or changing unrelated local configuration.
Integrate structured evidence at both local-gate and hosted-CI recovery boundaries, retaining the original caller revision and configured repository.
Wait on admitted or joined operations and return the verified target/rerun instruction through normal task integration without mutating the original branch or marking its gate green.
Suppress recursive repair under trusted repair-task context; retain ordinary handling for unsupported failure classes.
out_of_scope: General CI triage changes, automatic branch integration, scheduler enrollment, and activation before the incident and model-backed proofs.
acceptance: With routing disabled, existing local and hosted recovery fixtures retain their behavior; malformed or unknown configuration values refuse.
With routing enabled, the supported local and hosted memory failures call shared admission and produce zero independent memory-fixer edits while following the winning operation.

update_required preserves the target revision, verified successor, and rerun instruction through the local or hosted driver, worker outcome, and caller-visible result; caller work remains unchanged and its failed check is not silently marked successful.
Unsupported checker failures use the ordinary path, while a repair worker's own supported blocker remains on its task with no recursive launch.
key_interfaces: Closed memory.inherited_learning_repair.enabled setting, structured gate evidence, shared repair delegation, trusted repair context, and typed caller-adoption blocker.

implementation.rationale: A narrowly guarded branch changes the executor's local and hosted CI recovery path, so preserving the existing factory loop requires system-level assessment.

review.rationale: Review must establish that unrelated failures retain recovery, supported failures cannot launch independent memory edits, and repair tasks cannot recurse or bypass a red gate.

tasks.title: Prove five callers, concurrent scan, and stale adoption
tasks.goal: Reproduce the reported multi-agent failure and demonstrate one repair plus correct adoption across independent checkouts.
tasks.current: Individual seams can pass unit tests without proving the incident across processes, shared remote state, and stale caller tools.
tasks.desired: A retained-history fixture reproduces the unchanged inherited witness mismatch, observes one task and launch across five CLI processes and a scan, then proves fresh-target adoption after a valid successor lands.
scope: Build a hermetic incident history using the existing evidence helpers, local bare remote, and shared recording tracker/executor adapters.
Run five independent processes naming the same Learning ID from checkouts with different diagnostics, witnesses, and caller revisions while a scan competes through the same admission path.
Land a valid successor in the fixture and exercise a stale checkout, stale tracking ref, older caller verifier, and missing/incompatible verifier variants.
Exercise failure, ambiguity, cancellation, unresolved terminal state, injection, disabled routing, and recursive suppression while retaining exact preservation assertions.
out_of_scope: Live network in unit tests, a generalized memory corpus, model-backed success claims, and implementation of recovery or takeover.
acceptance: Five independent callers plus concurrent scan share exactly one task and one executor invocation, and reporting workers make zero independent memory repair edits; the fixture passes with the configured Go test command without race instrumentation, as directed by the operator's replacement repository instructions (problem:inherited-learning-repair#A-7).
After fixture landing, a stale caller receives update_required for the current verified target and successor with zero new tasks or dispatches; unavailable verification never reports fixed.

Fault and abuse fixtures preserve operation identity, caller HEAD, index and files, predecessor bytes and failed witness, and ordinary gate refusal without retries, recursive work, or allowance changes.

The advertised built and installed flows, adapter conformance, existing successor refusal suite, vet/lint, and fresh transport-clone validation pass at the reviewed revision with deterministic effect receipts.
key_interfaces: Retained-history incident fixture, independent process harness, shared effect receipts, installed command flow, and revision-bound verification evidence.

implementation.rationale: Construct a hermetic retained-history incident and independent-process effect receipts that exercise the real CLI and worker boundary.

review.rationale: The acceptance proof must detect process-local coordination, stale-tool false success, predecessor rewriting, and evidence-gate bypass rather than mirror the implementation.

tasks.title: Retain a bounded worker trial and document opt-in operation
tasks.goal: Demonstrate that the bounded charter produces a valid successor through the configured executor and make safe explicit operation understandable.
tasks.current: Hermetic effect receipts do not prove a model-backed worker can make the correction, and users lack supported-case and adoption guidance.
tasks.desired: One isolated retained-history incident trial uses the configured direct-issue executor and retains the exact candidate, independent review, and deterministic evidence; help explains explicit repair, wait, bounded daily invocation, opt-in routing, and deferred recovery.
scope: Run one model-backed incident trial through implement-now within existing configured execution and repair budgets, using isolated fixture history and the bounded charter.
Retain sanitized revision-specific candidate, executor, independent review, and evidence-verifier receipts at the owning evaluation/proposal.
Document explicit `--record Learning-<ULID>` repair and `--scan` for the known incident, caller adoption and tool revalidation, the opt-in setting, and disabled routing.
Keep automatic routing and scheduling disabled in shared defaults; activation requires the blocking incident and worker-trial evidence, not an inferred fixture-only success.
out_of_scope: New deployment hosts or schedules, broader repair cases, automatic merge, and abandoned-operation recovery.
acceptance: One configured model-backed trial yields an independently accepted successor candidate whose deterministic report retains the unchanged predecessor and original failed witness as historical-unresolved with a verified successor.

The retained trial identifies actual tool/route and candidate revision, ordinary verification and review outcomes, one dispatch, and zero unrelated edits, evidence bypasses, recursive dispatches, or automatic merges.

Published help demonstrates explicit request, shared wait, update_required with revalidation, bounded daily scan, and indefinitely stalled/uncertain operation limitations without claiming automatic recovery.
Disabled-routing rehearsal prevents automatic submissions while explicit invocation and existing operation observation still work; shared defaults and unrelated scheduling remain unchanged.
key_interfaces: Configured implement-now trial, EVAL-1 receipts, independent implementation review, evidence verification, explicit command help, and opt-in/disabled routing.

implementation.rationale: Exercise the existing configured model-backed path once in an isolated incident trial and retain real candidate, review, and verifier evidence.

review.rationale: Review must distinguish model-backed correction evidence from fixture success and ensure the opt-in guidance grants no new recovery or merge authority.
